subject: Scope consolidation & slab pricing change order — next steps
messages:
From: Emily Santos <esantos@novacorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Lowe <mlowe@novacorp.com>, procurement@novacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: consolidate SOW tasks + rework pricing slabs (draft attached)

Hi Irene / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As discussed with our engineering leads, we want to consolidate two implementation tracks in Exhibit B (feature integration + model tuning) into a single phased track to reduce coordination overhead. That consolidation changes the unit of work and shifts volume across the pricing slabs.

Attached is our proposed change (Novacorp_CO_Draft_v3.pdf) with the redlined Exhibit B and a short note from procurement on preferred billing cadence. High-level asks:
- Combine Implementation Track A & B into a single SOW section that still preserves the acceptance criteria.
- Adjust the slab thresholds so the committed throughput bands reflect expected steady-state (see comments in the draft).
- Keep current billing floor but allow a one-month credit for the consolidation transition.

Can Redwood send a formal change order/CO draft with your standard tracked changes and any legal caveats you need? We’d like to route this to internal legal/procurement next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Emily Santos
Procurement Manager, NovaCorp
attachments: Novacorp_CO_Draft_v3.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidate SOW tasks + rework pricing slabs (draft attached)

Emily — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. We can do a tracked-change change order from our side. Next steps from Redwood:
1) Legal will do a redline pass (Irene), focusing on acceptance language and rollback protections.
2) Finance will validate the slab math and propose equivalent fee mechanics to preserve commercial intent (Markus).
3) Sales/CS will validate operational impact and the proposed one-month transition credit (me / Karthik).

Irene — can you do the initial redline by EOD Tuesday 10/19? Markus / Karthik, copying you for slab/billing sanity check.

Emily, I’ve added a modest implementation-scope checklist in the HubSpot deal (link below) so we don’t miss milestone gating items. If all looks good we’ll send a DocuSign-ready change order for signature.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-19T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidate SOW tasks + rework pricing slabs (draft attached)

Laura / Markus — quick read-through notes after initial pass on Novacorp_CO_Draft_v3.pdf: 
- Acceptance criteria: the consolidated SOW must contain explicit test vectors and the rollback trigger (we should keep the original acceptance backstop language, but allow the consolidated steps to be staged). I inserted comments where the draft removed previously enumerated criteria — we should restore minimal language.
- Liability / data handling: Nova added a paragraph referencing "data residency options" — flagging that we need the standard DPA pointer rather than freeform language.
- Billing credit: procurement's request for a "one-month credit" is reasonable but the credit mechanics must be tied to invoiced tokens/throughput in the transition month and limited to the implementation fees, not ongoing consumption charges.
- Change-order template: please use our redwood_changeorder_template.docx to ensure we carry the right signature blocks and effective dates. I will produce an annotated redline and mark items that need commercial sign-off.

Inline example (from my notes):
> Draft phrase: "Acceptance shall be deemed when NovaCorp confirms delivery."
> Proposed legal: "Acceptance shall be deemed upon successful completion of the acceptance tests set forth in Exhibit B, or, failing that, ten (10) business days after delivery, unless Customer provides written notice of non-conformance."

I’ll circulate the annotated PDF by EOD. If procurement wants to preserve the original language for speed, call it out and we can propose a limited-term exception instead of permanent contract language.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Santos <esantos@novacorp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidate SOW tasks + rework pricing slabs (draft attached)

Team — I looked at the slab changes in the draft. Two quick commercial notes:
1) The proposed slabs shift ~22% of expected volume out of the mid-tier into the entry tier which reduces margin materially. We can preserve overall economics by adjusting the per-unit fee in Tier 1 by ~9%. I attached a simple matrix to show the equivalent fee moves.
2) We need to confirm whether the transition credit should reduce the upfront implementation invoice or be applied as a credit to the first monthly invoice after go-live. My preference is apply to the implementation invoice to keep ongoing consumption accounting clean.

Attached: pricing-slab-matrix.csv (model and suggested fee adjustments).

If procurement prefers to keep list prices steady, we can also propose a one-time implementation credit that flows through invoice adjustments (no change to the rate card). I’ll defer to Laura for the negotiation posture.

Markus Klein
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing-slab-matrix.csv

Subject: Re: Request: consolidate SOW tasks + rework pricing slabs (draft attached) — Redwood next steps

Emily / Michael — thanks for the patience and the clear draft. Quick summary and proposed timeline so procurement/legal have a single source of truth: 

What Redwood will do now:
- Irene will produce an annotated tracked-change CO using our change order template and restore minimal acceptance language in Exhibit B. (Irene -> will send annotated PDF tonight.)
- Markus will finalize the fee equivalency approach; we’ll include a note in the CO explaining whether the change is implemented via adjusted slab rates or a one-time implementation credit.
- I’ll prepare the DocuSign-ready change order and target sending to NovaCorp for signature by Friday 10/22.

Operational notes:
- Proposed effective / billing transition date: we suggest Nov 1, 2026 as the go-live month for the consolidated SOW. Implementation invoices will be adjusted per the agreed credit mechanism.
- HubSpot: I updated the deal with the CO checklist and added the DocuSign placeholder (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/9072).

Could you confirm (reply-all) whether NovaCorp is OK with: (A) Nov 1 effective date, and (B) implementation credit applied to the implementation invoice vs. the first monthly consumption invoice. If you prefer a quick call to resolve (A)/(B) I can schedule for tomorrow.

Once we have your confirmation we’ll push the tracked-change CO through and share the DocuSign link. Thanks — excited to get this locked in.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
